newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude, gas oil rise on U.S. weather.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude, gas oil rise on U.S. weather.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures tipped to the day's highs as some good fund buying came into a thin market. Fundamentally the impetus for the upward push came from forecasts for colder weather in the U.S., brokers said.

June Brent traded 37 cents firmer at 1230 GMT and stood at $18.29 a barrel, just off the intraday high of $18.32. Prompt May gas oil was last done at the day's high of $165 a tonne, a gain of $1.75 from Friday's settle.
"This is fundamentally led by the heating oil with the news of cold weather in the U.S. We are coming to test good resistance on the Brent now," one commented.

The call by OPEC president Abdallah el-Badri of Libya to restrain oil output was also market supportive, but traders would take a wait and see attitude. "It wont do much for prices until we see how people react," the broker added.
The next level of resistance on June Brent was at $18.35 a barrel and could prove difficult to push through, brokers said.
"But then it really depends on the Americans and how aggressive they are this afternoon," another said.
Independent forecasters Weather Services Corp. said temperatures in the U.S. were likely to remain below normal in the next ten days.

OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said on Monday that the OPEC president Abdalla el-Badri had called on its members to restrain oil output but it was not yet clear whether there had been any response to the request.
